lesson_title: Hot Sand, Cool Breeze: the Whole Atmosphere on One Beach
hook_text: The sand burns your feet but the air is mild. That one fact explains the weather.
clip_script: Go stand on a beach at one o'clock in the afternoon, barefoot. The sand is scalding, but the air around your shoulders is pleasant. If the sun heated air directly, the air would burn and the sand would not. It is the other way around because sunshine passes through air and lands on surfaces — the sand is the heater, and air only warms by touching it and rising off it. The atmosphere is heated from below. Now collect all four heat movers without leaving your towel. The warmth of the sun on your face is radiation — arriving across a hundred and fifty million kilometres of nothing. The burn on your bare soles is conduction — heat crossing by direct touch. Watch the air shimmer and wobble above the hot sand — that is convection, warm air rising in wriggling columns; the same columns, grown huge over the interior, stack up the afternoon thunderclouds. And at about three o'clock the sea breeze arrives, cool marine air sliding sideways onto the land — advection. Four beach sensations. Four processes. One heater, and it is under your feet.
visual_style: A sun-drenched beach scene built up in layers: heat lines radiating onto a face, a footprint glowing red, shimmer columns rising off the sand, then a broad cool arrow sweeping in from the sea.
mood: Warm, sensory and playful, sharpening into a clean lightbulb moment.
pacing: Languid beach beats for each sensation, then a quick four-word recap and a hard close on 'the heater is under your feet'.
call_to_action: Take the full lesson and see why mountains freeze, storms build and the sea breeze always knows when to arrive.
